name: GET /api/leadflow/sagas/{run_id} - the run and its step ledger
description:
Returns one saga run with its ordered step ledger: which steps ran, which were compensated, and which compensation itself failed.

THE LEDGER IS THE POINT, not the summary. A status field can say 'compensated'; only the ledger can say that step four was undone, step three's compensation ALSO failed, and step two is therefore still out there. That is what an operator reconciles a half-finished saga from, and it is why a failed compensation is recorded and the rollback continues rather than stopping - stopping would orphan every earlier step because a later one could not be undone, turning one orphan into a chain.

The run id IS the idempotency key, which is deliberate: it is derived from the business identity (deal plus charge, or platform plus source event), so an operator holding the deal id can construct the run id without a lookup table.

The run id is NOT invented here: it is captured from POST /api/leadflow/closed-won/start, which returns the idempotency key it ran under, and that endpoint is a dependsOn of this one. That is the producer chain MUST-36 asks for, and it is also the only honest way to read a run back - a fabricated key matches nothing and 404s.

Behind authenticate and governed on onboarding.manage, held by client_success alone, so the definition declares requiresRole:["admin"] and the runner swaps to testCredentials.admin (qa.operator@leadflow.test, whose local `admin` role bridges to client_success). QA: depends on register and login.

NO testCase sets its own Authorization header, and that is required rather than stylistic: an explicit header takes PRECEDENCE over the role token, so declaring requiresRole and then pinning a header means the role token is never sent and the endpoint 403s (MUST-71). The two 401 cases were removed for the same reason - they can only be expressed by overriding the header, which would defeat the swap. They remain documented in errorCases below, and the 401 branch is middleware behaviour identical across all 51 routes, already covered by the definitions that do not declare a role.

testCases.name: Read back the run that closed-won/start just created, with its step ledger
NEGATIVE: a well-formed run id that matches no run

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify

errorCases.message: No saga run with that id
errorCases.when: no run exists under that idempotency key. Reachable now that the definition runs as admin, and covered by the {{var:absent_saga_run_id}} case.

errorCases.message: No policy grants this action to the caller's roles.
errorCases.when: the caller's roles do not grant onboarding.manage. NOT reachable while this definition runs as requiresRole:["admin"]; the DEFAULT suite identity bridges to sales_rep and receives exactly this.
